text.text: The Sinclair ZX81 was released in 1981 as an affordable home computer designed to introduce users to programming. It used a minimal hardware design with a Z80 processor, membrane keyboard, and black-and-white television output. The system was sold as both a kit and assembled computer, making it accessible to hobbyists and students. Software was distributed mainly through cassette tapes and magazines. The ZX81 helped expand interest in personal computing and was followed by the more advanced ZX Spectrum.
